context: campus-scale central utilities · phased building-by-building handover

brief.intro: New to this project type? A university campus is really several buildings — teaching blocks, laboratories, a library, residences — fed from one shared central utility plant for chilled water, power and data. Unlike a single school, the programme has two tiers: get the central plant and campus-wide distribution live first, then commission each building off it. Laboratories add a genuinely technical layer — fume extract, lab gases, specialist HVAC — that a normal teaching block doesn't need. Because the campus usually opens in phases rather than all at once, the schedule really is several linked but separately-paced sub-projects sharing one backbone, and the central plant is the thing that gates every one of them.

scope.desc: Chilled-water plant, standby power and the main incoming substation feeding the whole campus.

scope.desc: Chilled-water ring main, HV/LV ring main and the data/telecom backbone between buildings.

scope.desc: Foundations, frame, roof and envelope for each teaching, lab and residence block.

scope.name: Building MEP fit-out
scope.desc: HVAC, power and plumbing inside each block, tied into the campus mains.

scope.name: Laboratory services
scope.desc: Fume extract, lab gases, specialist HVAC and containment for science/engineering buildings.

scope.name: Fire & life safety
scope.desc: Detection, alarm and suppression per building under one campus-wide fire strategy.

scope.name: ELV / security / IT backbone
scope.desc: CCTV, access control, structured cabling and the data backbone linking every building.

scope.name: External works & landscaping
scope.desc: Quads, walkways, sports fields and parking.

scope.name: Testing, commissioning & phased handover
scope.desc: Central plant proving first, then building-by-building commissioning and occupancy.

glossary.plain: the campus's own power/cooling "power station" that every building draws from.
a looped power or chilled-water main serving multiple buildings from one source.
piped gases (compressed air, vacuum, specialist gases) serving science/engineering labs.
ducted exhaust removing hazardous lab fumes from a fume cupboard.
the campus-wide fibre network every building's data system plugs into.
opening finished buildings one at a time rather than waiting for the whole campus.
the controls system that manages plant and building services campus-wide.

must_get_right: The central plant must be live and proven before any building can be meaningfully commissioned off it — sequence it first, not last.
Laboratory services are a specialist scope (fume extract, gases) — don't treat a lab building like a generic teaching block.
Plan and contract for phased, building-by-building handover from day one — it drives the whole logic network, not just the finish line.
The campus IT/telecom backbone must land early enough for each building's fit-out to tie into it, not wait for it.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. The campus is modelled as a central-plant sub-network feeding a series of per-building sub-networks, each with its own commissioning and handover milestone.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Structure runs a standard single- or two-shift week; central plant and campus distribution run extended shifts to protect the network's gating milestone; commissioning runs extended hours ahead of each phased opening.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs central-plant procurement → substation/chiller set → campus ring mains energised → first building tie-in & commissioning → phased occupancy. Laboratory buildings carry their own sub-critical path through fume-extract and gas commissioning that must clear before lab occupancy, independent of teaching-block readiness.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Design freeze per building, phased occupancy dates agreed with the university client, the central plant sized and released for construction ahead of individual buildings, and free-issue lab equipment coordinated by others. Any change to the central-plant delivery date cascades into every building behind it.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Multiple buildings under construction concurrently compete for the same finishing trades; campus roads and laydown are shared across contractors. Once early phases open, later-phase work may need to sequence around a live, partially occupied campus.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Central-plant slippage is the principal risk — it cascades into every building behind it, so contingency is held before plant energisation rather than spread across building fit-outs. Laboratory re-test loops (face-velocity, containment) and phased-handover slippage are tracked separately per building so one late block doesn't delay others.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (campus-wide milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3 per building; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for laboratory and central-plant commissioning — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
